bibl.title: Discovery and quantification of plastic particle pollution in human blood

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: PLASTIC PARTICLES IN HUMAN BLOOD - a quantity nobody had measured, in a literature where the two available names for the particles do not have settled definitions
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether plastic particles cross into the human bloodstream at all, and whether a method sensitive enough to say so can be built
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the first mass-concentration measurement of polymers in human blood - 1.6 ug/ml across 22 donors - and the double-shot Py-GC/MS method that produced it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: existence
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: plastic particles absorbed across membranes and present in circulating blood, at a rate exceeding whatever removes them
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: double-shot pyrolysis gas chromatography/mass spectrometry on whole blood from 22 healthy volunteers, targeting particles retained on a 700 nm filter
span.term: double-shot pyrolysis gas chromatography/mass spectrometry on whole blood from 22 healthy volunteers, targeting particles retained on a 700 nm filter
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE INFERENCE THE NUMBER LICENSES IS A RATE COMPARISON, NOT A QUANTITY: finding particles in blood `indicates that ... THE RATE OF ELIMINATION via e.g. the biliary tract, kidney or transfer to and deposition in organs IS SLOWER THAN THE RATE OF ABSORPTION into the blood`. A standing concentration is evidence about two rates and about neither one alone
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the paper is careful about what the blood compartment is: it `REMAINS TO BE DETERMINED whether plastic particles are present in THE PLASMA or are CARRIED BY SPECIFIC CELL TYPES`. `In blood` is a location, and the mechanism of carriage is not in evidence
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: blood is the transport route: it irrigates the organs, so a particle that enters it can reach tissues, and its fate is renal or biliary elimination or deposition in liver, spleen or other organs
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: capillary diameter sets a physical ceiling on what can circulate, and anything at that size would itself affect microvascular flow
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: particles may be localised in immune cells, stuck to proteins, lipids, each other or the vessel wall - so a mass concentration can be real while duplicates disagree
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE CONSTRUCT'S BOUNDS ARE TWO PHYSICAL OBJECTS AND THE PAPER SAYS SO BEFORE REPORTING A NUMBER: `our OPERATIONALLY DEFINED method targeted particles that could be retained on A FILTER WITH PORE SIZE OF 700 nm ... THE INNER DIAMETER OF THE NEEDLE used for venipuncture (0.514 mm) can be considered the UPPER SIZE LIMIT`. Everything below a filter pore and above a needle bore is outside the finding by construction
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE INSTRUMENT DECIDES WHAT EXISTS: `POLYPROPYLENE WAS ANALYSED BUT VALUES WERE UNDER THE LIMITS OF QUANTIFICATION`. Absent from the blood and absent from the instrument are the same sentence here, and the study cannot separate them
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the two available names for the object DO NOT HAVE SETTLED DEFINITIONS: `microplastic` has `NO UNIVERSALLY ESTABLISHED DEFINITION` and is `often defined as ... up to 5 mm WITH NO DEFINED LOWER SIZE LIMIT`, while `nanoplastic` means <1 um in this literature and `<100 nm` IN THE NANOTECHNOLOGY FIELD. ONE WORD, TWO FIELDS, TWO THRESHOLDS
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the sample is 22 donors and the paper calls it what it is - `A SMALL SET OF DONORS` - in the same sentence as the headline concentration
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the result is explicitly NOT a risk statement: `no absorption models can be validated and NO STATEMENTS ABOUT RISK OR NO RISK CAN BE MADE` without measured internal exposure data. The measurement is a precondition for the question, not an answer to it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the PM2.5/PM10 convention of reporting an operationally defined mass concentration per unit volume is adopted wholesale as the way to quantify plastic in blood
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the size window is fixed and declared before any measurement - a 700 nm filter pore below, a 0.514 mm needle bore above
span.note: eliminates: any reading of the number as a total; it is the mass of what falls inside two physical limits, and the paper states both · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether polypropylene is absent from blood or below the assay's threshold
span.note: eliminates: nothing, and the sentence cannot be made to: `POLYPROPYLENE WAS ANALYSED BUT VALUES WERE UNDER THE LIMITS OF QUANTIFICATION` · outcome: failed
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether the measurement supports a risk claim
span.note: eliminates: the risk reading, explicitly and in both directions: `NO STATEMENTS ABOUT RISK OR NO RISK CAN BE MADE` without measured internal exposure data - which this study provides for the first time and which is still only the precondition · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: drawing blood through a closed all-glass vacutainer system with a steel needle and no plastic tubing or reservoir
span.note: eliminates: plastic contamination introduced by the sampling equipment itself, which would manufacture the very finding being sought · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: identifying the rubber vacutainer seal by ATR-FTIR to establish which polymer it is
span.note: eliminates: the possibility that the one unavoidable non-glass component contributes to the targeted polymers · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: running the entire sampling system as a field blank before any sample
span.note: eliminates: background contamination attributable to the collection apparatus rather than the donor · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: duplicate extraction and measurement of each sample where volume allowed, with multiple procedural blanks per series
span.note: eliminates: single-measurement artefacts and uncorrected background drift between series · outcome: held

span.label: `plastic particles` - A TERM THE AUTHORS COIN FOR THEIR OWN USE, because the field's two names will not hold still: `TO CIRCUMVENT THE AMBIGUITY of the terms microplastic and nanoplastic particles in this article WE WILL REFER TO plastic particles AND WHERE APPROPRIATE DEFINE THE SIZE OR SIZE RANGE`. The remedy for an unstable term is to stop using it and carry the number instead
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `microplastic` - `NO UNIVERSALLY ESTABLISHED DEFINITION EXISTS`, and the common one - up to 5 mm - has NO LOWER BOUND AT ALL. A term whose extension is open at one end
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `nanoplastic` - <1 um in this literature, `<100 nm` IN THE NANOTECHNOLOGY FIELD. ONE NAME, TWO FIELDS, A TENFOLD DIFFERENCE IN THE THRESHOLD, and the paper reports both rather than choosing
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `a plastic particle in blood`, AS OPERATIONALISED HERE - anything retained on a 700 nm filter and small enough to pass a 0.514 mm needle. THE CONSTRUCT IS BOUNDED BY A FILTER PORE AND A NEEDLE BORE, in the authors' own words, and the phrase they use is `OPERATIONALLY DEFINED`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `under the limits of quantification` - what the paper reports for polypropylene, and the one phrase in the record that cannot be read as a fact about blood. It is a fact about the assay
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: extends → Leslie and Depledge's and Vethaak and Legler's position that a human health risk assessment for plastic particles is not currently possible for want of exposure data
